newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian Sugar - Thai raw sugar premiums seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar - Thai raw sugar premiums seen firm.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums are expected to be firm for a while due partly to concerns over possible tight supplies next year, Japanese traders said on Friday.
"The raw sugar crop in Thailand next year may be damaged as the dry weather has taken its toll on production," a trader at a major trading house said.
"Thai sugar premiums will stay firm for a while as moderate demand is emerging in addition to the supply concerns," he said.
Traders said, however, activity was generally lacklustre as China was still out of the market.

Thai raw sugar premiums for July/September deliveries were quoted a tad firmer at around 80/90 points (bid/offer) per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange futures on an FOB basis, compared with 85/95 earlier this month.
Traders said there are expectations that the Philippines will step into the market to buy about 300,000 tonnes of sugar later this year.
